newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Melbourne Cup and Golden Slipper winning jockey Darren Beadman yesterday announced he would retire at the end of the year in order to become a minister with the Christian Life Centre, claiming God instructed him. Page 19.

Carlton captain Stephen Kernahan suffered a badly strained left calf which could end his season as his team was defeated by Adelaide 18.19 (127) to 13.8 (86) in their Australian Football League clash at Football Park yesterday. Page 21.

Illawarra ended Parramatta's 11-game winning yesterday, with the Eels just one game short of equalling their club record. Illawarra defeated the Eels 28-24 to remain in contention for the Australian Rugby League finals series. Page 28.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

News Limited executive Ian Frykberg said yesterday that Australian Rugby League chairman John McDonald had met with he and colleague Lachlan Murdoch to be brought up to date about the peace negotiations between Super League and the ARL, after being left out of official talks to date. Page 32.

Lawyers from Soccer Australia and Sydney United will meet today in an attempt to avoid a court battle over the Sydney team's future in the Ericsson Cup, which has been in danger since they were found guilty of bringing the game into disrepute at a preliminary final last season. Page 34.

The Sydney Sandpipers netball team will meet the Sydney Swifts in the minor semi-final of the Commonwealth Bank Trophy after defeating Adelaide 59-52 yesterday to earn fourth place in the national netball competition. Page 35.
THE AGE

Sydney Swans star Tony Lockett may be cited by the Australian Football League Tribunal today for a controversial collision in his team's clash against Melbourne on Saturday. The clash left defender Shaun Smith unconscious. Page 9.

Three-time Australian touring car series title winner Peter Brock drove in his final championship race yesterday in front of a record crowd of 45,000 at Sydney's Oran Park. Brock won the first of the three races, but blew a tyre in the last, with two laps to go. Page 18.

The Australian men's under-23 basketball team defeated South Korea 81-61 in a world championship game at the Glasshouse in Melbourne last night. The team struggled to maintain their performance after the break, when they held a 49-27 lead. Page 19.
THE HERALD SUN

Glenn Seton won the Australian touring car championship for the second time yesterday, finishing on 668 points, clear of John Bowe in second with 608 points and Russel Ingall in third on 572 points. Page 80.

A series of swab tests by racing stewards has resulted in the six month disqualification of Alice Springs trainer Catriona Green, three days after leading trainer Viv Oldfield claimed his team had been nobbled. The swabbing blitz will continue at today's Darwin Cup. Page 82.

Western Bulldogs president David Smorgon said yesterday the team's players found it hard to deal with the closer scrutiny they were under from rival Australian Football League clubs when they emerged as a contender for a finals position. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New South Wales rugby union officials have moved swiftly to draw up a contract for former Australian under-21 captain Ben Kennedy, who left the Waratahs last season to join the Canberra Raiders Super League team. Page 31.

The Sydney to Gold Coast yacht race record was smashed by more than seven hours when Sydney pocket maxi Foxtel Amazon finished the race at 8.12 pm last night. The yacht averaged faster than 15 knots, sailing in near-perfect conditions all the way. Page 32

The Australian Rugby League will continue to oppose the use of video referees despite a proliferation of controversial refereeing decisions. ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker and referees co-ordinator Mick Stone both say it is too late in the season to introduce the new system. Page 35.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
